title: Session affinity split during proxy upgrade leads to transient authorization 'ghost' access for Dedicated/Private customers
creator: Maya Chen
description: After a rolling upgrade of edge proxy instances in the APAC Dedicated cluster, customers reported intermittent 403s and, in a few sessions, unexpected access to tenant-scoped resources that should have been denied. The pattern was transient and correlated tightly with the proxy canary rollout. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix to prevent session-affinity splits during control-plane upgrades for Dedicated and Private deployments.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy proxy binary v2.12 -> v2.13 as a rolling upgrade with canary enabled on a Dedicated cluster.
2) Use a synthetic workload that pins requests from the same client to different backend nodes (simulate L4 LB rebalancing).
3) Rapidly rotate API keys for one tenant via the admin API while requests are in flight.
4) Observe 403s on some requests and in ~0.5% of flows, requests authenticated against stale in-memory binding succeed against the previous org-scoped cache entry.
impact_summary: Support spike: 18 customer escalations (mid-market + 3 dedicated enterprise tenants). Error rate: 4x increase in 403s for the cluster for ~7 minutes; ~0.5% of sessions observed anomalous authorization allowing access to resources cached on previous node (no data exfiltration verified). Affected: Hosted-like control plane in private mode and Dedicated nodes behind customer-managed LB configurations.
mitigation:
- Immediate: paused the canary rollout and rolled back proxy cluster to v2.12, which eliminated further anomalies.
- Short term: forced session cache flush across all nodes (+coordination with infra to invalidate in-memory apikey-tenant bindings).
- Workaround for customers: recommended edge stickiness by client-source-ip when available and advised delaying key rotations during cluster upgrades.
root_cause_analysis: During the rolling proxy upgrade, a subset of proxied requests were rebalanced mid-flight from an upgraded proxy to an older backend node with a cached apikey->tenant mapping that had not yet been invalidated. We rely on local in-memory session caches to reduce auth lookups; however, cache invalidation for key rotation and proxy-induced session migration were non-atomic. The upgraded proxy introduced a header rewrite optimization that removed a supplemental opaque cookie used by the prior node to validate freshness, so the older node accepted the request using its stale mapping. Race: (1) LB reassigns connection mid-request during upgrade, (2) new node strips freshness cookie, (3) old node honors in-memory mapping — leading to 'ghost' authorization windows.
implementation_notes:
Planned fix (3-phase):
1) Short-term patch: modify proxy rewrite logic to preserve the freshness cookie (X-Session-Freshness) and treat its absence as 'unknown' rather than 'fresh' so older nodes can't assume validity. Add a guarded auth-lookup fallback that double-checks TTL on apikeys for requests arriving without the cookie. (Target: +2 days)
2) Mid-term: move apikey->tenant binding to a small consistent distributed store (etcd-backed cache with <200ms read) that supports atomic invalidations on rotation. Provide an opt-in flag for Dedicated/Private customers. (Target: +4 weeks)
3) Long-term: LB-aware rolling upgrades — integrate a pre-drain signal to ensure session stickiness or graceful connection draining where possible. Add canary gating metric for in-flight auth error delta. (Target: +3 months)
Implementation will include unit tests for cookie-preserving rewrites, an integration test that simulates LB reassignments, and an e2e scenario with key rotation during upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy no longer strips X-Session-Freshness during upgrade (verified in canary)
Synthetic LB reassignments + key rotations do not produce 403 spike or ghost authorizations in integration test
Distributed cache prototype returns <=200ms P95 for apikey lookups in Dedicated test harness
Operational runbook updated and added to Dedicated upgrade checklist
Post-deploy monitoring dashboard (per-cluster auth-error-delta) added with alerting threshold
